pack.name: Charters and Corsairs
pack.summary: Far holdings: scouts find ore and timber in the hills, colonies pay while they stand, neighbours can be fed, frightened or bought into swearing to you, and the Gull Reavers can be paid, hired, pointed at your rivals, betrayed or burned out. A rival league takes whatever you leave alone.

factions.name: the Gull Reavers
factions.text: Sea raiders who sail from a hidden cove, take what they can and sell it where nobody asks.

factions.name: the Tollmark League
factions.text: A league of salt and toll towns down the coast. It buys what it cannot take, and takes what nobody holds.

leaders.name: Steward Hal Brook
leaders.line: Your steward in a far town that is yours. The run is played from there; your old town is a far town.

leaders.name: Captain Merrow
leaders.line: Once a Gull Reaver. She sails from their haven, and the sea raiders call her captain.
leaders.hint: Find out where the black sails come from.

between_runs.say: The Tollmark League bought the nearest free town. It swears to the League now.
The League cut the tracks to your camps, and no ships came. Their people left.
The towns of the old Sea League went their own ways. Its tithe stopped.

tags.meaning: Ships from up the coast call here.
Towns you fed send their young to work your streets.
Your factors buy the harvest of the towns sworn to you.
The Gull Reavers leave you alone and pay you a cut.
You pay the Gull Reavers every season to keep off.
This town sells its harvest freely in your market, and swears to nobody.

things.name: The Reavers' toll
things.text: A chest goes down to the beach every season: 1 Materials, so the Reavers keep off.
things.art: A small chest left on a beach at dawn, a black sail far out, painterly.

things.name: Sea charter
things.text: Ships sail between your waterside and the nearest towns while it stands.
things.art: A wax-sealed charter pinned to a harbour post, small sailing ships beyond, painterly.

things.name: The grain debt
things.text: The towns you fed remember it. Their young come to work in your streets.
things.art: Young travellers with bundles walking into a walled town at dawn, painterly.

things.name: Trading house
things.text: Your factors buy the harvest of every town sworn to you. Their wagons come here.
things.art: A tall timber trading house with a crane over the market square, wagons below, painterly.

things.name: The Reavers' bargain
things.text: The Reavers leave your ships alone, sell their loot in your market and pay you a cut of what they take.
things.art: Rough sailors haggling at a market stall heaped with mismatched goods, painterly.

cards.title: Send scouts over the ridge
cards.pitch: Shepherds talk of red stones in a valley past the ridge. Give me a few hands and I will find it.

if_taken.say: The scouts come back with red stones in their packs and a map.

if_expires.say: League prospectors find the red stones first and build a camp there.

cards.art: Two scouts on a ridge at dusk pointing at a red-rocked valley, painterly.

cards.title: Follow the river to the pine hills
cards.pitch: Logs come down the river every spring, too big for any wood we know. Pay me and I will pole up to see where.

if_taken.say: The ferryman finds a hillside of pines older than the town.

if_expires.say: League woodcutters float the first great logs past your quay.

cards.art: A flat barge poled up a misty river towards huge pines, painterly.

cards.title: Settle {find}
cards.pitch: {find} is ours if we go now. Families, tools, two seasons of work, and it pays every season after.

if_taken.say: Your people raise huts at {find}. The first carts start down the track.

if_expires.say: League settlers move into {find} while you wait.

cards.art: Settlers raising log huts on a hillside, carts of tools, painterly.

cards.title: The League claims {colony}
cards.pitch: League men stopped my carts on the track to {colony}. They say the land is theirs. Send soldiers or lose it.

if_taken.say: Your soldiers turn the League's men back from {colony}.

if_expires.say: The League's men take {colony}. Its carts stop coming.

cards.art: Armed men blocking a mountain cart track, a wagoner arguing, painterly.

cards.title: Take back {town}
cards.pitch: {town} is in other hands. Give me soldiers for two seasons and it flies our flag.

if_taken.say: Your soldiers raise your flag over {town}.

if_expires.say: {town} stays in their hands. People ask why you let it go.

cards.art: Soldiers climbing a palisade under a new banner, painterly.

cards.title: Send grain to {town}
cards.pitch: {town} had a bad harvest. Send them our surplus and they will not forget who fed them.

if_taken.say: Carts of grain roll to {town}. Its council swears to you out of thanks.

if_expires.say: The League feeds {town} instead. It swears to the League.

cards.art: A line of grain carts arriving at a hungry hill town, people cheering, painterly.

cards.title: March on {town}
cards.pitch: {town} pays nobody. Show it our spears and it pays us 2 a season.

if_taken.say: {town} opens its gates to your spears and swears.

if_expires.say: {town} laughs at your banners from its walls.

cards.art: A column of spearmen before a small walled town, gates opening, painterly.

cards.title: Buy up {town}'s harvest
cards.pitch: Buy their whole harvest for two years and {town} cannot sell to anyone else. Then it is ours.

if_taken.say: {town} sells only to your factors now, and swears to keep it so. Your own bakers grumble at the price of flour.

if_expires.say: {town} sells to the League. Prices rise in your market.

cards.art: A factor counting coins over sacks of grain under a trading-house crane, painterly.

cards.title: Open your market to {town}
cards.pitch: Let {town} sell its grain here, free of tolls. It owes us nothing, and our streets eat well every season.

if_taken.say: {town}'s carts come to your market every week. Nobody can buy up a town that sells to everyone.

if_expires.say: {town}'s carts go to the League's markets. Bread costs more in your streets.

cards.art: Farm carts unloading grain in a busy free market, a weaver watching, painterly.

cards.title: The League courts {town}
cards.pitch: League envoys passed me on the road to {town} with gifts. They mean to take it from you.

if_taken.say: Your envoy outbids them. {town} stays sworn to you.

if_expires.say: {town} swears to the League. Its tribute goes down the coast.

cards.art: Envoys with gift chests on a muddy road, a carter watching, painterly.

cards.title: Open a sea lane
cards.pitch: Ships pass us by. A charter and some work on the moorings, and they call here.

if_taken.say: Ships begin to call from up the coast.

if_expires.say: The ships go to other ports. The fishermen grumble.

cards.art: Sailing ships tying up at a busy wooden quay, painterly.

cards.title: Strange sails off the point
cards.pitch: Black-sailed boats come round the point at night. Let me follow them with a spyglass and a fast boat.

if_taken.say: Your lookout follows their sails to a cove up the coast where the Gull Reavers live.

if_expires.say: Black sails come and go. Nobody knows from where.

cards.art: A lookout with a spyglass on a tower, dark sails on a moonlit sea, painterly.

cards.title: The Gull Reavers want a toll
cards.pitch: A Reaver came ashore under a white rag. Pay 2 Materials now and 1 every season after, he says, or they take what they like.

if_taken.say: The Reaver takes the chest and bows. Their boats keep off your ships, while the chests keep coming.

if_expires.say: The Reavers burn their white rag and take the nearest port on the coast. Fewer ships call.

cards.art: A pirate under a white rag on a beach, a chest at his feet, painterly.

cards.title: Reavers at the waterside
cards.pitch: Boats on the water, torches in them. Six of them are coming for the quay.

triumph.say: Not one boat gets away. Their loot is yours.

success.say: The Reavers row off, leaving a boat full of loot.

cost.say: They are driven off, but not before they empty a warehouse.

failure.say: The Reavers fire the waterside and row away laughing.

if_expires.say: Nobody stands on the quay. They loot it at their leisure.

cards.art: Torch-lit rowing boats landing at a quay at night, defenders running, painterly.

cards.title: Make a standing deal with the Reavers
cards.pitch: The truce holds. Go further: let them sell their loot here and raid the League's ships, and take a cut of every town they hold.

if_taken.say: Reavers walk your market in daylight now. The League's ships stop coming.

if_expires.say: The truce lapses. Their sails are just sails again.

cards.art: A castellan and a pirate captain shaking hands over a map, painterly.

cards.title: Point the Reavers at {town}
cards.pitch: The Reavers ask where the fat towns are. Tell them {town}, and the cut of it comes to you.

if_taken.say: The Reavers sail on {town}. Its people come to your gate with what they carried.

if_expires.say: The Reavers find their own prey and keep all of it.

cards.art: A smuggler whispering to a pirate among old gravestones, painterly.

cards.title: Hire the Reavers against the raid
cards.pitch: The raiders come by the shore road. The Reavers could meet them at sea first, for 5 Materials of my best iron.

if_taken.say: Reaver boats now watch the shore road. Fewer raiders will reach you.

if_expires.say: The Reavers sell their oars to the raiders instead.

cards.art: A smith handing new axes to grinning sailors, painterly.

cards.title: Hand the Reavers to the League
cards.pitch: The Reavers drowned my son. The League pays 6 Materials for their haven and 1 every season after, and our soldiers know the way.

if_taken.say: League ships take {haven} while the Reavers sleep. The League calls you friend.

if_expires.say: The League hears you trade with pirates.

cards.art: A miller's lantern guiding warships into a sleeping cove, painterly.

cards.title: Follow them home to {cove}
cards.pitch: The boats that fled went home to {cove}. I saw the way. Two seasons, and it burns.

if_taken.say: {cove} burns. The town drinks to it in the streets.

if_expires.say: They rebuild their boats at {cove}.

cards.art: A pirate cove burning at night seen from the sea, painterly.

cards.title: Raise the Sea League under your flag
cards.pitch: Three towns or more answer to you already. Call them all to one league, under one flag, and the coast is ours.

if_taken.name: The Sea League sails under your flag

if_taken.say: Every standing town on the coast swears to the Sea League. Your flag flies from every mast.

if_expires.say: The towns drift apart again, each to its own.

cards.art: Ships of many towns flying one banner in a crowded harbour, painterly.

cards.title: Copy the old survey maps
cards.hint: Scouts who come back with a map could leave it for whoever leads next.
cards.pitch: Our scouts drew maps of the ore and the pines years ago. Pay a clerk to copy them and we know where to go.

if_taken.say: The clerk copies the maps. Redscar and Tall Pines are on your table again.

if_expires.say: Damp gets into the map chest. The scouts grumble about walking the ridge again.

cards.art: A clerk copying faded maps by lamplight, painterly.

cards.title: Hire a Reaver pilot
cards.hint: A pirate who knows the coast might work for you, once you know where pirates live.
cards.pitch: An old Reaver wants honest pay. He knows every cove on the coast. 2 Materials and he guides our ships.

if_taken.say: The pilot takes your ships into coves nobody charted. Three towns trade with you by sea.

if_expires.say: The pilot sails for the League instead, and tells them what he saw here.

cards.art: A weathered sailor at a ship's wheel pointing at a hidden cove, painterly.

cards.title: Hang the old League banner
cards.pitch: We found the banner of the Sea League in a chest. Hang it in the shrine and the coast will remember whose it was.

if_taken.say: Captains from the old league towns come to see it, and to trade.

if_expires.say: The banner rots in its chest.

cards.art: A faded sea banner hung in a mountain shrine, candles, painterly.

rules.name: The mill saws the timber
rules.why: the mill saws the logs of {count} colonies: +{n} Materials

rules.why: {count} towns sworn to you pay tribute: +{n} Materials

rules.why: ships from {count} towns unload at the quay: +{n} Materials

rules.name: Follow them home
rules.why: the boats that fled showed the way to {a}

events.title: Reavers at the waterside
events.how: Cast fire into the boats as they land. Each cast puts down a Reaver.

laws.name: The Reavers row for the raiders

wants: Boats: a live event group that comes from the water (sea side of the harbour) in boats, not on foot from a site.
A far event: the Reavers' raid on a far town played as a live event there, not only as a card's effect.
Founding by the coast: a pirates' haven placed on the shore, a colony placed on its ore, not round the hills.
Arrive from a far place: refugees from a town the Reavers took walking in from that town, not from the neighbour.
A faction acting by itself each season (the League buying up an ignored town) without a card to carry it.
